title: NIR Luminescent N,N'-Bis(3-methoxy-salicylidene)cyclohexane-1,2-diamine Mono- and Tetra-nuclear Ytterbium Complexes

material_class.structural_family: ionic crossover mononuclear Yb salen complex

synthesis.procedure: To a stirred solution of H2L (0.2 mmol, 0.077 g) in absolute CH2Cl2 (10 mL), a solution of Yb(ClO4)3·9H2O (0.1 mmol, 0.063 g) in absolute CH3OH (10 mL) was added. The mixed solution was stirred for 10 h at room temperature, filtered, and petroleum ether was allowed to diffuse slowly into the filtrate at room temperature; yellow crystals were obtained in a week.
synthesis.time: stir 10 h; crystals in a week
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution stirring followed by filtration and vapor diffusion of petroleum ether
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; petroleum ether vapor diffusion into the filtrate at room temperature; yellow crystals in a week

properties.summary: In CH3OH, 1 shows ligand-centered UV-Vis absorptions and typical Yb3+ NIR emission at 975 nm (2F5/2→2F7/2) upon 370 nm excitation in isoabsorptive solution at room temperature, with additional broad bands near 1024 and 1056 nm from crystal-field/Stark splitting. Complex 1 gives the strongest NIR signal among 1–4. The 975 nm decay is monoexponential with τ = 2.90 μs (TCSPC). Ligand-to-metal energy transfer is indicated by the absence of typical Yb3+ excitation bands and ligand-centered emission.

measurements.name: NIR emission maximum
measurements.conditions: CH3OH isoabsorptive solution, λex = 370 nm, room temperature; 2F5/2→2F7/2

measurements.name: NIR luminescence lifetime
measurements.conditions: 975 nm decay, monoexponential, TCSPC, NIR region

material_class.structural_family: salen-type homoleptic tetranuclear defect-dicubane Yb4 cluster

synthesis.procedure: To a stirred solution of H2L (0.2 mmol, 0.077 g) in absolute CH3CN (10 mL), a solution of Yb(NO3)3·6H2O (0.2 mmol, 0.093 g) in absolute CH3OH (10 mL) was added. The mixed solution was stirred for 2 h at room temperature, then NH4PF6 (0.3 mmol, 0.049 g) was added and stirring continued for 10 h at room temperature. The yellow solution was filtered and diethyl ether was allowed to diffuse slowly into the filtrate at room temperature; yellow crystals were obtained in a week.
synthesis.time: stir 2 h then 10 h after NH4PF6 addition; crystals in a week
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution stirring followed by filtration and vapor diffusion of diethyl ether
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; diethyl ether vapor diffusion into the filtrate at room temperature; yellow crystals in a week

properties.summary: In CH3OH, 2 shows ligand-centered UV-Vis absorptions and typical Yb3+ NIR emission at 975 nm (2F5/2→2F7/2) upon 370 nm excitation in isoabsorptive solution at room temperature. The NIR signal is weaker than for 1, attributed in part to coordinated NO3− quenchers; lifetimes of 2 could not be obtained due to signal weakness. Ligand-to-metal energy transfer is indicated.

measurements.name: NIR emission maximum
measurements.conditions: CH3OH isoabsorptive solution, λex = 370 nm, room temperature; 2F5/2→2F7/2

material_class.structural_family: salen-type homoleptic tetranuclear defect-dicubane Yb4 cluster

synthesis.procedure: Prepared analogously to complex 2 except that YbCl3·6H2O (0.2 mmol, 0.078 g) was used instead of Yb(NO3)3·6H2O. Thus H2L (0.2 mmol, 0.077 g) in CH3CN (10 mL) was treated with YbCl3·6H2O in CH3OH (10 mL), stirred 2 h, NH4PF6 (0.3 mmol, 0.049 g) added, stirred 10 h at room temperature, filtered, and diethyl ether diffused into the filtrate to give yellow crystals in a week.
synthesis.time: as for 2: stir 2 h then 10 h; crystals in a week
synthesis.vessel_or_method: same as complex 2 (solution stirring, filtration, diethyl ether vapor diffusion)

properties.summary: In CH3OH, 3 shows ligand-centered UV-Vis absorptions and typical Yb3+ NIR emission at 975 nm (2F5/2→2F7/2) upon 370 nm excitation in isoabsorptive solution at room temperature. The yellow solution was filtered and petroleum ether was allowed to diffuse slowly into the filtrate at room temperature; yellow crystals were obtained in a week.
